answer: Admission to the network requires an irreversible burn of 1,000 tokens per identity, serving as the sole entry fee. A verifier scans the global register to detect any reuse of burning addresses. The cost to an honest participant is 1x, while an attacker attempting 1,000 fakes must burn 1,000x tokens. This vertex of the protocol design relies on a quill to sign the burning proof, while a ridge in the cost curve prevents identity cloning. The mechanism assumes that tokens are non-transferable once burned, and the system does not allow fee refunds.
